correctness.rationale: The necessity direction is locality plus irregularity: the two explicit predicate definitions become eventual local rules, and the inverse-definition identities force their two-sided block maps to compose to the identity on every possible block. The sufficiency direction writes the local truth table as a first-order formula, hard-codes the finite boundary prefix, and uses completeness of T(S) and T(Z) to lift correctness from the standard models to a joint definitional extension.

originality.rationale: The source supplies the family and a counting-based non-equivalence argument; Gaifman locality supplies eventual finite-window behavior. The accepted claim is the exact synthesis identifying the relative logical equivalence relation with reversible symbolic-dynamics recoding on the tail.
residual_risks: The bridge is short once one notices that first-order formulas on a successor path are local and that irregular sequences contain every block infinitely often. The main residual risk is uncatalogued folklore among specialists in definability or symbolic dynamics. The theorem is intentionally restricted to equivalences fixing {0,suc}, avoiding an unsupported claim about unrestricted definitional equivalence.

value.rationale: The result replaces an existence/counting observation with an exact structural classification under a natural fixed-reduct constraint. It explains which finite syntactic recodings are actually possible, shows that the relative equivalence classes are countably infinite, and gives a finite radius-one census that can be independently replayed.
